client_brief:
We are opening Lesson 4 of Operations Analytics for Working Managers to people who have not bought the course yet. The recorded lecture and screen captures we can hand over are five seconds each and none of them carry audio, so a narrated lesson excerpt is not something we can honestly ask for. What we want instead is a course teaser: a short, plain piece that shows the real screens and puts the teaching line on screen as text, the way a working manager watches video on a laptop at midnight with the sound off.

The commission

1. Course teaser: 1 named export, 12 to 15 seconds, 16:9, under the supplied instrumental bed (meridian_bed.wav). It names the lesson, states the topic, and carries two teaching lines lifted word for word from the approved caption sheet. The screen captures must stay readable: give a viewer time to see what is on the screen before the next cut.

2. Course teaser vertical cutdown: 1 named export, 6 to 8 seconds, 9:16, silent, cut from the same material. Set the landscape screen captures inside a framed panel on a brand ground rather than cropping into them, so the interface keeps its own proportions and stays legible upright.

3. Lesson cover: 1 named export, unchanged from the register.

House rules for this package

- No voice. Nothing in this package is narrated and no deliverable carries speech. The message is carried by on screen text you author from meridian_captions.csv and meridian_lesson4_outline.txt.
- Do not invent teaching copy. If a line is not in the approved caption sheet or the outline, it does not go on screen.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage: looping one short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table. Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Practical skills for people who already have a job.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A four person team running one course.
brand_identity.about: Meridian Academy sells a single self-paced program, Operations Analytics for Working Managers, at two hundred and ninety dollars. Our learners are thirty to fifty, mid-career, watching lessons late at night after their own workday. We are not a bootcamp and we are not a university. We teach one useful thing well and we respect the viewer's time and intelligence.
brand_identity.audience: Working managers aged thirty to fifty, paying with their own money, fitting the course around a full-time job. They want a working skill, not a transformation story, and they distrust anything that feels like marketing.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-market. A two hundred and ninety dollar considered purchase. The register sits between an impulse-priced tutorial and a formal institution: competent, quiet, self-funded professional development.
brand_identity.typography: Meridian Academy runs two faces and four steps. Step 01, display, is the lesson numeral in Larish Neue Medium at 280 px on 294 px leading, tracking -12 units, Cream Stock on Deep Slate and cropped by the left frame edge. Step 02, the subheading, is the lesson topic in Larish Neue Medium at 96 px on 104 px leading, tracking -8 units, stacked beside the numeral and dropping to 72 px on the vertical cutdown. Step 03, body, is Untitled Sans Regular at 54 px on 68 px leading, tracking 0, set to a maximum of 65 characters a line on teaching cards. Step 04, fine print, is Untitled Sans Regular captions at 38 px on 48 px leading, tracking +8 units, with the lesson label one step above it in Untitled Sans Medium at 34 px. Certificates sit outside the screen scale: the crest sets in Larish Neue small caps at 22 pt, tracked 120 units, over a 1.5 pt rule, and never in a sans.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, matter of fact. Speaks to a peer, not a beginner. Short sentences, no hype, no exclamation. The tone of a good colleague explaining something over coffee.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Brand files are largely gone. When we changed studios the original crest design file was lost, and the mark now survives only on the completion certificates we had printed two years ago: an enclosed laurel ring with small caps type set inside it and a rule beneath, in one deep ink on cream stock. We would like it recovered as artwork we can use at any size. No usable logo vector, colour spec sheet or type licence exists on our side.
brand_identity.values: Respect for the learner's time, honesty about what the course does and does not cover, and production that is clear and quiet rather than loud.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Every lesson card opens with an oversized Larish Neue lesson numeral in Cream Stock on Deep Slate, cropped by the left frame edge so a third of the figure runs off screen with the topic stacked beside it.

type_system.signature_move: Every lesson card opens with an oversized Larish Neue Medium lesson numeral at 280 px, Cream Stock on Deep Slate, cropped by the left frame edge so a third of the figure runs off screen with the 96 px topic stacked beside it.
rules: Never typeset the crest in a sans.
Certificates set the crest in Larish Neue small caps at 22 pt, tracked 120 units, over a 1.5 pt rule.
The oversized lesson numeral is never fully inside the frame; the left frame edge always crops about a third of it.
The lesson topic drops to 72 px on the vertical cutdown; every other step holds.
The lesson label sets in Untitled Sans Medium at 34 px; teaching cards and captions stay Untitled Sans Regular.
No exclamation and no hype in any line set at any step.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
source_of_truth: Approved client notes and permissions govern factual corrections. V4 output register governs commissioned output classes and sizes. Original rows are not automatically approved copy.
